channel.title: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?" - Im writing a story where a helpful reality bender accidentally neutralizes SCP-106 during a containment breach. What award would somebody get for that?

item.title: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded: Well, I do enjoy the Scarlet King lore, so perhaps 2317 would be a good idea for neutralization? I have no idea but maybe the Foundation will spare him if he terminates 2317.

item.title: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded: I think it's also depend on how they did it. If it's something that disgust Ethics Committee, the reward is likely to be "bullet to the head".

item.title: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded:
Well, there's the Foundation Star, as shown here: SCP-1983. However, they were only rewarded for the neutralization given that this was an incredibly dangerous anomaly that was quite possibly impossible to contain and chewing up agents.

You could also say that readers didn't mind them breaking that "rule" because it was a good story.

IMO, if your story is about a reality bender being awarded for accidentally neutralizing a anomaly (which most readers don't think would be rewarded), and you're just picking between the most well-known Keters on the site, maybe read more of the wiki? That might be a hard story to pull off unless you have more lore to build from and know what current readers enjoy.

item.title: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded:
None, because again, wrong precedent to set. The Foundation isn't a videogame entity that awards points for destroying things.

ETA: that is, per my headcanon anyway. Other readers may disagree.

item.content:encoded: I'm not certain that such an action would be officially rewarded, given that the Foundation's general anti-neutralization if they can manage it. If neutralization were some sought-after thing then it would have been attempted under laboratory conditions.

item.title: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded: If someone were to accidentally neutralize a keter, the foundation would be extremely suspicious. Heck, scp 181 just survived a keter twice and they knew something was up. I'm assuming your story is gonna cover that, but just know the research into him would be extensive. As for an award, they would probably give him quite a few leisure privileges, potentially letting him choose his assignment, potentially a pay raise, and likely other things you would expect from exceeding well in a job. Keep in mind that that's all for if the foundation actually wanted the thing dead, if they wanted to experiment with it more, he could potentially even get punished for neutralizing it.

item.title: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded: As you heard from the summary, I am writing a story in which a doctor who is a reality bender and does not want others to find out he is a reality bender. What award would somebody get if someone were to accidentally neutralize a keter during a breach?
